dimensions.note: git diff 27c2b0b HEAD adds no credential, env read, token or secret field; rg for Deno.env/token/apiKey in extensions/lib/evidence.ts and ci.ts finds none. realTests still starts deno with no env option (evidence.ts:357-370), so the app's tests inherit the reviewer's environment and whatever -E/-A ci.yml names reaches it. That is unchanged by design; the over-grant cases under api-contracts make it matter more. (carried from round 1) (carried from round 2) (carried from round 3)

The release adds no logger calls. readiness still logs on entry and around scoring (draft.ts:3181, 3214, 3236) with structured placeholders; rg for template-literal logger calls under extensions/models finds only a test of guarded() (draft_test.ts:859). The new reason for a refused or unread tests command reaches the user through the summary (readiness.ts:460, clipped at 200 chars) and the blocker 'The app's tests could not be run: ...' (readiness.ts:568-571), not a log line. (carried from round 1) (carried from round 2) (carried from round 3)

Round 4 (git diff f5f05cc HEAD): the new refusal 'takes a permission set but is not a single plain deno test command' (evidence.ts:358-369) returns {error} through unsupported() before deno starts, with the full command at the end of the message, like the other refusals (evidence.ts:301-305). It applies only when a permission set is present (evidence.ts:349, 363), so a line without -P keeps its old outcome. Ran /tmp/review-r23d/h/probe.ts: 'deno test -A extensions/ 2>&1 | tee log', 'deno test -R extensions/ && cd docs && ls' and 'deno test -RW extensions/' are still accepted with the same permissions as sh -c. Round 3's small gap ('cd sub & ...' refused though harmless) now also covers any harmless line with -P, such as 'deno test -P extensions/ 2>&1' or 'deno test -P extensions/;'. The owner accepted that, and the upgrade note says so (draft.ts:2143-2147).

Ran deno fmt --check (Checked 112 files, exit 0) and deno test -A --permit-no-files (661 passed, 0 failed, 29s). The new test (evidence_test.ts:199-254) pins all five round 3 lines and other separators, redirections, a newline, a leading variable and a trailing & as refused. It also pins plain -P, -RP=ci, --permission-set=ci, a continuation/comment line and a CR line as accepted, and keeps the --config/--no-config/&> checks. Small gap: the refusal assertion accepts either 'single plain deno test' or 'changes directory' (evidence_test.ts:239-246), so the new rule is not tested on its own for cd lines such as 'cd sub & ...'. The '{ cd sub; }', 'if', 'command', 'eval' and '!' lines can only pass through the new rule, so they do test it.

shellCommands and testPermissions are still pure functions of ci.yml (evidence.ts:197-271, 296-371). The new plain flag and used-count check add no state or I/O, and a rerun on the same checkout gives the same flags or the same refusal.

Round 3's issue is fixed. I compared real sh -c (dash, /bin/sh -> dash) with deno run on readiness's flags (deno test <flags> extensions/models/ from the root). I used HEAD's extensions/lib copied to /tmp/review-r23d/lib, /tmp/review-r23d/h/probe.ts with l1-l5.json, a root deno.json whose test.permissions grant everything plus a 'ci' set of read only, sub/deno.json {}, and a Deno.permissions.query probe. '{ cd sub; } && deno test -P extensions/', 'if true; then cd sub; fi; deno test -P extensions/', 'command cd sub && ...', 'eval cd sub; ...' and '! cd sub; ...' are all refused (evidence.ts:361-369). These were accepted and gave the same permissions as sh: plain 'deno test -P extensions/', '-P=ci', '-P=default', '--permission-set', '--permission-set=ci -N ... -- -A', a quoted "'deno' \"test\"", 'de\<newline>no te\<newline>st -P', continuations with a trailing '# -A' comment, a leading '# cd sub' comment line, '# ; cd sub', trailing and leading newlines, a tab, a trailing CR and '-P\r' (deno ignores the CR). A reserved word or builtin as the only command ('exec deno test -P', '{ deno test -P extensions/ }') is not a deno test run, so it gets no flags and no permission set. Smaller gap, older than this release (the .trim() at evidence.ts:300 dates from 795dec7) and not in #147/#157/#161: JS trim() strips a trailing or leading Unicode space that sh keeps in the word. 'deno test -P=ci -E=HOME\u00a0' gives readiness env HOME granted, but sh gives it prompt (it grants 'HOME\u00a0'). 'deno test -P\u00a0' gives readiness every permission, while CI fails with "Could not find permission set ' '". A leading U+FEFF makes CI exit 127. Each case needs an invisible character, and readiness grants more than CI, so readiness can pass where CI fails. A fix would be to trim only space, tab and newline. Other DIFFs in the probe were path-only (readiness always tests extensions/models/, an older design), not permissions.

The diff adds no process, file or timer. The only process is still the Deno.Command with stdin null, piped output and a 300 s AbortSignal (evidence.ts:400-412), and the new refusal returns before it starts. (re-checked in round 4)
The diff adds only test strings (extensions/, sub, log, x, j) and upgrade-note prose (evidence_test.ts:199-254; draft.ts:2143-2147). It adds no host, IP, ID or secret.

TestRun.note is a TypeScript-only field (evidence.ts:42-43) and is not persisted: readiness stores only tests {passed, failed} (readiness.ts:645-649). The 2026.11.23.1 upgrade note (draft.ts:2143-2147) now says that readiness takes a permission set (-P, --permission-set, and so deno.json's test permissions) only from a single plain deno test command, with no other command, separator, redirection or variable set for it, and refuses any other line with -P, even a harmless one. That matches evidence.ts:358-369. upgradeAttributes is still identity, and the version is unchanged. Small wording gaps: 'any other line with -P' also means -RP and --permission-set, which the sentence before names. Comments, line continuations and blank lines around the one command are still accepted, which 'no separator' does not quite say. The new sentence starts with a lowercase 'readiness' after a full stop. The string line at draft.ts:2147 is longer than its neighbours, but deno fmt --check passes.
